reviewUnits.section: TrustLink Labs / TSN > Native wallet-to-TIN credit architecture
reviewUnits.excerpt:
The first transaction transfers sender assets into the TCAP reserve; the
second advances confidential state after independent settlement verification.
Receiver pre-creates settlement work at ingress but gates verification on
confirmed funding. Credit does not pay a recipient wallet. If settlement fails,
its state mutations roll back; the earlier confirmed deposit remains separate.
An expired owner-signed funding wire requires fresh wallet approval and a
new signature, and a stale proof/root or lease requires re-verification rather
than reuse of the old execution projection.

reviewUnits.section: TrustLink Labs / TSN > Core terms and authority boundaries
reviewUnits.excerpt:
Receiver stores restricted durable work and coordinates leases/status; it does
not make the Node's verification decision. Node resolves routes and checks
funding/proofs. Cranker validates the signed execution projection and submits
the permitted transaction. Mother authority co-signs inspected settlement
through Mother Escrow; its key/role differs from Node decision signing. Solana
validators supply execution, ordering, consensus and finality. The
[component reference](docs/laboratory/components.md) covers SDK, identity,
epoch/DNA, ingress and external integration responsibilities separately.

reviewUnits.excerpt: For Solana’s ElGamal key format, if the stable public key is \(P=s^{-1}H\), Node can choose a random \(r\), publish \(E=rH\), and compute the shared point \(S=rP\). The owner computes the same \(S\) from \(E\) and their secret. Both derive a tweak \(t\) from \(S\) and the unique DNA, then use one-time public key \(P\_{\text{DNA}}=tP\); the owner recovers its matching secret as \(s/t\). Solana’s implementation defines its public key using the inverse secret scalar, which is why the matching secret derivation takes this form. reviewUnits.section: GPRU Memo delta proof finding > Resolution
reviewUnits.excerpt: For a private scan scalar `s`, TIP registers `S = s * Base8` in the authenticated route leaf. Each action chooses a fresh private scalar `e`, publishes `E = e * Base8`, and publishes `C = delta + x(e * S) mod q`. The Groth16 witness uses this same `delta` in the Pedersen successor and proves the ciphertext equation. GPRU binds `C` and `E` to the Memo prefix and hashes the complete Memo. The owner computes `delta = C - x(s * E) mod q` and uses the recovered value when replaying the decrypted action history.

reviewUnits.section: GPRU portfolio and proof contract
reviewUnits.excerpt: This contract aligns the hidden-head circuit, settlement Memo, and owner balance recovery. reviewUnits.section: Historical TSN epoch and opaque-slot settlement architecture
reviewUnits.excerpt: The Node/Mother keeps the payment binding (recipient route, sender refund destination, funding lineage, amount, mint, epoch, and payment hash) in encrypted storage. The encryption key and plaintext never leave Node/Mother. A keyed slot is derived by authorized Node/Mother with HMAC-SHA256 and is withheld until settlement or refund.

reviewUnits.section: Historical TSN epoch and opaque-slot settlement architecture > Mother-rooted DNA
reviewUnits.excerpt: For a lease, Node signs a permit binding the opaque slot, commitment digest, random nonce, nullifier, Mother-rooted epoch treasury and ledger, CrankerVault, recipient, mint, amount, lease id/version/expiry, and authorization expiry. The `EpochClaimSlot` PDA is derived from the epoch treasury and opaque slot. It is initialized by the first valid settlement or refund, so the slot first appears on chain at that operation. It stores no payment id, sender, or recipient identity beyond the public payout coordinate required by the transfer.

reviewUnits.section: Historical TSN epoch and opaque-slot settlement architecture > Mother-rooted DNA
reviewUnits.excerpt: The first successful operation wins. Settlement atomically checks the Node permit, lease, slot state, nullifier, and treasury liability; pays the recipient from the CrankerVault; reimburses that exact CrankerVault for the exact amount; marks the slot `SETTLED`; and records the successful Cranker. Refund uses the same slot and marks it `REFUNDED`, returning the exact amount from epoch treasury to the Node-authorized refund destination. A later operation against the same slot fails before token movement.

reviewUnits.section: Historical Mother-rooted epoch settlement architecture
reviewUnits.excerpt: Mother authority materializes the one-time `SettlementDna` PDA at the derived slot. 6. No admin path can move user funds; the router holds nothing between transactions.
7. Pause blocks new deposits only; burned intents still complete.
8. All accounting in 6-decimal ERC-20 units, never the 18-decimal

recipient set to the **TSN reserve**, and emits an intent keyed by that commitment. On Solana, CCTP mints
into the reserve and TSN credits the recipient's private balance. The only link between the two chains is
the `routeCommitment` plus the Node's records.

reviewUnits.section: Cranker transaction submission map > Work, transaction and instruction boundaries
reviewUnits.excerpt: A Receiver work item is a durable service task. A transaction is a signed message submitted to a chain and identified by a signature or transaction hash. Instructions execute inside that transaction; a cross-program invocation (CPI) lets one Solana program call another without creating a new transaction. One TIN work item can therefore produce several upload transactions, while one native-credit transaction can execute TSNP, TCAP, GPRU and Memo instructions atomically.

reviewUnits.section: Cryptographic mechanisms and privacy boundaries > Pedersen balance and recoverable delta
reviewUnits.excerpt: Balance commitments use additive BabyJubjub points. A credit adds the amount contribution and a fresh blinding delta contribution to the selected token point. The authenticated TIP route includes the owner's scan public point `S = s * Base8`. The action publishes `E = e * Base8` and the field ciphertext `C = delta + x(e * S) mod q`. The circuit constrains those values to the same private delta used in the balance transition. The owner recovers `delta = C - x(s * E) mod q` with owner-held scan material.

reviewUnits.section: Protocol invariants, state changes and recovery > Root, nullifier and accounting continuity
reviewUnits.excerpt: TCAP checks active/approved asset policy, pause state, sufficient pending liability and reserve solvency. After GPRU verification, it subtracts the same amount from pending liability and adds it to settled confidential liability while advancing the shared root. This instruction does not make a new token payout to the recipient. If proof verification or any check fails, the root/accounting mutations in that transaction roll back together.

reviewUnits.section: EXP-20261101: binding the owner delta to the proved transition > Problem and hypothesis
reviewUnits.excerpt: The earlier design hashed a Memo carrying an independently encrypted blinding delta. Hashing those ciphertext bytes did not prove that the decrypted delta was the one used in the Pedersen successor. An owner could therefore receive a decryptable record that did not permit consistent balance replay. The revised hypothesis was that the circuit must prove an owner-recoverable ciphertext relation using the exact transition delta.

reviewUnits.section: EXP-20261101: binding the owner delta to the proved transition > Revised setup and implementation
reviewUnits.excerpt: TIP registers the scan point `S = s * Base8` in its authenticated route. Each action selects fresh private scalar `e`, publishes `E = e * Base8` and `C = delta + x(e * S) mod q`, and constrains that relation in the circuit. The same delta appears in the additive Pedersen successor. Owner SDK recovery computes `delta = C - x(s * E) mod q` and rejects payloads attempting to supply another delta.

reviewUnits.section: EXP-20261102: verifier initialization packet limit and staged setup > Problem, replacement and contract
reviewUnits.excerpt: The current proof requires twelve public inputs and thirteen IC points. The original initializer encoded two 32-byte commitments, a 64-byte alpha point, three 128-byte G2 points, a four-byte IC vector length, thirteen 64-byte IC points and an eight-byte instruction discriminator: 1,356 bytes of instruction data against a 1,232-byte transaction packet limit. A lookup table cannot remove the instruction-data payload. The superseded direct initializer therefore had no usable client transaction.

reviewUnits.section: TIN V1 Creation Flow > Wallet recovery and resolver boundary
reviewUnits.excerpt:
The wallet is the user's ownership and authorization anchor. The TIP program
creates a single owner-indexed recovery PDA and rejects creation when that
owner already has an active TIN. The PDA contains only an encrypted recovery
envelope. On a new device, the SDK fetches it by owner PDA and uses a fresh
signature over the recovery message to decrypt the TIN locally; newly created
records use V4 envelopes. The SDK also retains read-only V2/V3 decryption for
existing records. None of these steps writes a plaintext `wallet -> TIN` index.

reviewUnits.section: TIN V1 Creation Flow > Wallet recovery and resolver boundary
reviewUnits.excerpt:

operational boundary and must be configured before exposing a resolver to
untrusted callers. Identity lookup alone does not authorize owner actions or
reveal a settlement transaction graph.

reads the Creditcoin registry again during the transaction, checks the EIP-712
authorization, rejects replayed settlement IDs and nonces, reserves capacity,
and calls the executor. The executor can release only from the configured
vault.

reviewUnits.section: Cranker TIN-operation job > What changed
reviewUnits.excerpt:
The daemon accepts `TIN_OPERATION` work only after verifying the Node's Ed25519
receipt with `TSN_NODE_VERIFICATION_PUBLIC_KEY`. It checks the active lease and
input/evidence commitments, then recomputes the exact Cranker execution-payload

reviewUnits.excerpt:
Public blockchains make payment verification simple by publishing accounts and
transactions. The same model also exposes durable relationships between
wallets. This paper argues that payment privacy cannot be solved by encryption
alone. Identity, authorization, receiving, settlement, and confidential asset
control must be separated so that unnecessary relationships are not created in

reviewUnits.excerpt:
TSN receives signed payment intent data, verifies it, creates eligible work,
leases one execution opportunity to a Cranker, and verifies the resulting
settlement. The Receiver stores durable non-secret work. The Node makes
off-chain verification and routing decisions. The Cranker submits exact
authorized work and pays fees. The TSN Program enforces on-chain signatures,
commitments, leases, replay protection, and token movement.

authorizes an intent on an authorized device. The Receiver stores durable
non-secret work, the TSN Node verifies and resolves the destination, and a

enforces the final commitment, lease, replay, and token-account rules.

reviewUnits.section: TSN Node by TrustLink Labs > Deployment
reviewUnits.excerpt:

Receiver/Firebase poll. The Receiver sends an authenticated, payload-free
`POST /internal/wake` after committing new work. The Node then drains the
queue and sleeps again. A single startup drain handles work that arrived while
the Node was offline. If the Receiver is unavailable or the service credential
is invalid, the Node uses bounded exponential backoff and returns to the same
event wait after six failed attempts instead of burning CPU indefinitely.

reviewUnits.section: TSN Receiver by TrustLink Labs > Runtime boundary
reviewUnits.excerpt:
When the optional Realtime Database wake channel is enabled, the Receiver also
writes a control marker to `tsn/crankerWake`. The marker contains only a nonce,

Database stream, receives the marker, then calls `/api/cranker/work` to lease
verified work from Firestore. Firestore remains authoritative for work,
leases, idempotency, replay state, and results; the wake marker is never a
work payload. If the channel is unavailable, Crankers use bounded fallback
backoff rather than failing a durable submission.

reviewUnits.section: createLitSolanaTinMasterSeedProvider > LIT_SOLANA_TIN_ACCESS_READINESS
reviewUnits.excerpt:
Lit's current Solana AuthSig proves control of a Solana address, but the
pinned SDK does not provide a verified device-bound capability flow that
prevents a captured Solana AuthSig from being presented by another client.
Its normal Solana access-control decryption is directly wallet-gated; the
local TSN device proof is not evaluated by those threshold nodes.
Master-seed protection must fail closed until that second factor is enforced
by the threshold network, not merely checked by this browser process.

reviewUnits.section: Current native-credit sequence
reviewUnits.excerpt: For settlement, Node resolves the TIP route, reads current roots/verifier, reconstructs root-matching witness snapshots, encrypts the Memo action, generates and verifies a local proof, and rechecks chain preconditions. It signs the exact execution projection. Cranker obtains authorization and Mother co-signing for its current lease, then submits the TSNP call followed by the bound Memo. TSNP invokes TCAP; TCAP invokes GPRU before advancing the shared root and shifting equal liability from pending to settled confidential state.

reviewUnits.section: How reserve protection works
reviewUnits.excerpt: TCAP tracks the actual assets held for each accepted token and the obligations recognized against those assets. A wallet deposit increases the vault assets and the reserve's funded pending liability together. When a private credit is accepted, TCAP moves the credited amount from pending liability to settled confidential liability. For example, a funded 100 USDC can support an 80 USDC credit, leaving 20 USDC pending and 80 USDC settled; the total recognized obligation remains 100 USDC.

reviewUnits.section: How reserve protection works
reviewUnits.excerpt: The funding limit is pooled per asset, not restricted to deposits from the same epoch. TCAP rejects a credit when its amount exceeds funded pending liabilities or when recognized liabilities exceed the recorded reserve assets. The proof-gated credit also checks the current shared commitment root and sequence. GPRU verifies the private-state transition; only then does TCAP advance the root and update the liability counters atomically. If a check fails, the transaction rolls back, so the root and reserve accounting are not partially advanced.

TCAP must apply that same proven amount to its accounting. This is why a proof is not a fund authorization on its own and why the proof statement and TCAP transition must agree.

reviewUnits.excerpt:
- **TIP** manages transfer identity and route information. Wallet recovery uses an encrypted record separate from the main TIN registry account.
- **GPRU** guards the integrity and privacy of the user's private state presented to TCAP. A proof is not a payment authorization or a funds key.
- **TCAP** governs accepted assets and reserve liquidity, and applies valid authorized changes atomically.
- **Cranker** submits authorized transactions and pays their network fees. Fee payment does not grant authority to edit the transaction's terms.

1. Preserve the request identifier and any transaction signatures.
2. Query the latest request status and inspect each transaction on the selected network.
3. Do not retry with altered sender-approved terms.
4. If an owner-signed transaction has expired, prepare a new one and request the owner's signature again.

reviewUnits.section: Core boundaries
reviewUnits.excerpt:
- **The owner authorizes wallet actions.** A service or Cranker cannot change the sender's signed payment terms.
- **GPRU guards private state.** Its proof is intended to show that the hidden user state is current and that the proposed transition follows from it.
- **TCAP governs funds.** It checks accepted assets, authorization, and liquidity, then applies valid changes atomically.
- **A confirmed transaction is the settlement evidence.** Request acceptance, service verification, and transaction submission are earlier stages.

reviewUnits.section: Participant boundaries
reviewUnits.excerpt:
| Participant | Role | Boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Sender wallet | Reviews and authorizes the payment. | A service or Cranker cannot replace the sender's approval. |
| TSN services | Coordinate and verify payment work. | Service acceptance or verification is not on-chain settlement. |
| Cranker | Submits authorized work and pays transaction fees. | Submission does not prove confirmation or give authority to alter payment terms. |
| GPRU | Guards the user's private state presented to TCAP. | A proof does not hold funds or replace TCAP checks. |
| TCAP | Governs accepted assets and applies

reviewUnits.section: Participant boundaries > Identity privacy and public-chain visibility
reviewUnits.excerpt: The native-credit ABI hides the recipient route/head witness and does not encode a plaintext TIN or private predecessor pointer. The owner retains its record lineage. Shared roots, public statement fields, encrypted Memo bytes, accounts, timing and funding wallets remain observable; the design does not establish that metadata or authorized Node/application knowledge cannot correlate payments. Confidential debit/exit remains a separate unverified execution path.

reviewUnits.section: Participant boundaries > Identity privacy and public-chain visibility
reviewUnits.excerpt: The current Node derives the published credit nullifier from the public deposit signature and TCAP program ID using a domain-separated SHA-256 hash reduced to a BN254 scalar. An observer can recompute the funding-to-credit relationship without a secret. This protects the deposit replay context but limits transaction privacy; it does not reveal the hidden TIN witness by itself. Node also handles private routing/witness preparation, so owner-only knowledge is not established.
